content:
Great effort getting into Warrior One—well done for holding the posture. I can see you’re grounding down and engaging your legs, which is fantastic. Let’s refine it a bit to help you get even more strength and alignment in the pose.

First, let's address your spine. Right now, it’s slightly curved, which can compress the lower back. To fix this, gently draw your navel in toward your spine and lengthen through the crown of your head. Imagine a straight line running from your tailbone all the way up through the top of your head. This will create a long, neutral spine and help you feel more steady and supported.

Next, your arms—right now they’re reaching up but not quite vertical. To improve this, reach your arms actively toward the sky, bringing your biceps alongside your ears. Keep your shoulders relaxed down your back and energize through your fingertips as if you’re lifting your arms toward the ceiling. This will help elongate your sides and open your chest.

Finally, check your front knee—it’s starting to drift a bit forward of your ankle. Your knee should be directly stacked over your ankle to protect the joint and maximize strength. Soften your front knee slightly if needed and draw it back until it’s aligned with your ankle. This will give you a stronger foundation and more power in the pose.

You're doing really well—just small adjustments are going to make a big difference. Let’s take a breath in, and as you exhale, realign your knee, lift through your arms, and lengthen your spine. Beautiful—there it is! Hold it here with awareness. Keep breathing deep, steady breaths. You’ve got this.
